evidence: errorMiddleware(error, _req, res, _next) uses Express Request/Response/NextFunction and sends a response with res.status(...).json(...). This is HTTP transport work, which belongs in infrastructure.
STATUS_BY_KIND: Record<DomainErrorKind, number> maps domain error kinds to HTTP status codes 404/409/400. It translates errors for the transport and makes no business decision.

parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/errorMiddleware.ts is an Express error-handling middleware. Its one job is to turn thrown errors into HTTP responses. That is transport and framework work, and it belongs in the infrastructure layer. The STATUS_BY_KIND table maps abstract domain error kinds (not_found, conflict, invalid) to HTTP status codes. That is presentation mapping, not business logic. The domain decides what kind of error happened, and this file only decides how it looks over HTTP. The file holds no business rules, no persistence and no application orchestration.
